AgentTerm

Steer a fleet of the coding agents you already run: beyond the terminal, on surfaces you already know.

Use with any CLI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc).

Coding agents chose the terminal for a reason: nothing is more flexible, and everything composes with it. But the terminal never caught up to what the agent became. Everything an agent prints (a diff, a plan, a claim, a link) is dead text you can read but not act on. And once you're running several, each is an identical tab outside and a wall of text inside, with no telling which you meant to get back to. AgentTerm keeps the foundation and breaks through the ceiling: act on what the agent prints, review what it built until it's right, find the right session, steer it mid-run. Where that takes conventions that don't exist yet, it defines them as open protocols: the agent prints a review:// link, and the review opens right in the terminal.

Point at anything the agent shows you (a line of terminal output, or a diff) and say what you want; the agent makes the change.

Find the right session

Run many agents and AgentTerm tracks them at two levels. The ones you're actively juggling become Windows taskbar buttons, each with a working indicator and two levels of live preview showing what the session's for and what it's doing. (On a Mac, run each session full screen: each window pins its initial prompt at the top, readable in a Mission Control swipe.) The ones you've set aside are a keystroke away: open the picker and filter your past sessions by what you asked them, or what the agent called the work, while a deeper pass searches every prompt you typed; resume any of them (the hero above). No hunting through look-alike terminals, and no back-and-forth with an agent to find it for you.

Watch and steer from your phone

Add the companion viewer (agent-stream-hub) to your phone's home screen as a web app. It shows which agents need you across all your machines ("your turn"), and drills into any live session as the terminal itself: the same screen you left at your desk, recognizable at a glance, with even its menus drivable key-by-key. Steer it by voice: speak, and your words reach the agent as text it knows came from voice, so it repairs the mishears and false starts against the session before acting. That's the part phone dictation can't do: with no view of your code it hears "pie test" and leaves it there; the agent turns it into pytest. Type instead, even from a network that only allows outbound HTTPS.

   

Plus the quality-of-life stuff

Paste images and drag-drop files straight into a prompt · fuzzy-search the whole scrollback · click an image path the agent prints and it renders right in the app (Ctrl/Cmd-click sends .pdf, .csv, folders and the rest to their OS apps) · right-click to quote a selection into the prompt. Ctrl+K / Cmd+K inserts your IDE's current location into the prompt.

Comment on its output

Most of what an agent tells you scrolls past in the terminal. Select any of it (a line, a claim, a command it's about to run) and comment; your note goes back to the agent with the exact text quoted, so a few words are enough. (Works on the rendered markdown viewer too.)

If your CLI captures the mouse (Claude Code's fullscreen rendering does), hold Shift while selecting; commenting works the same. To keep plain-drag selection, launch Claude Code with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS=1 to keep its wheel scrolling.

…and what reaches the agent: your words, with the exact context quoted:

Review, not a wall of diff

When the agent finishes, it prepares your review: it hands you the parts that need your judgment, ordered and explained with trade-offs flagged, and leaves out what doesn't need it: the mechanical noise (renames, imports, boilerplate) and what you already settled during the session. Comment inline, on the code and on its reasoning; it edits, replies in the thread, and the review re-renders in place.

Plan with it

The viewer turns markdown into a place you write English, live. A doc opens rendered and updates as the agent works. Comment on any passage, or edit the rendered text directly, starting new lines anywhere; edits reach the agent as suggestions, and it decides what each new line becomes in the source (a heading, a list item, a paragraph). You write in the preview, never touching raw markdown or switching edit/preview modes, and the agent maintains the source.

And English is where the real planning happens. A large part of design is settled in words before any code: the plan, the design doc, the findings. Those docs are how you work with the agent, and how you work with other people. They become so fast to produce this way that one project can carry a targeted doc for each audience: for the agents, for developers, for program managers, and more. The plan converges the way code does: commented, revised in place, settled before anything is built. The same loop covers any writing project (essays, notes, research, docs): your materials are organized as a repo the agent uses as needed and edits for you.

Confirm what the agent tells you

Agents explain themselves by quoting file:line and symbols. Ctrl-click any reference the agent mentions (Cmd on Mac; not just files it edited) and your IDE jumps to that exact line so you can verify the claim. URLs it cites open too, in an embedded web view right in the terminal.

Look without breaking it

Your IDE editor stays read-only by default, so you don't have to worry about a stray keystroke. (Flip a setting on the rare occasion you want to edit directly.)

Make it yours

Everything here is modular and agent-sized: the terminal is 18k lines of plain JS (MIT), and the IDE plugin, phone viewer, and review spec are each their own small repo. Take the piece you want and make it your own. Share what you build, and pull in what others make.

Platform

Runs on macOS and Windows. AgentTerm is built on a Mac using AgentTerm itself, and used heavily for work on Windows, so both are first-class. Live-session switching is integrated with the Windows taskbar. On a Mac, give each session its own full screen or desktop: the initial prompt stays pinned at the top of the window, so a Mission Control swipe shows every session, readable (a more Mac-optimized UX is welcome). IDE navigation targets JetBrains today, but the protocol's open, so other editors and code viewers are easy to add. PRs welcome on both fronts. All MIT, all free: no telemetry, no upsell.

How it works (for the curious)

  • One click rule: a plain click opens what renders in-app (markdown, reviews, web pages, images); anything that hands you to another application (OS apps, your IDE) waits for Ctrl/Cmd; commenting always goes through a selection.
  • Append-only, single-pass decoration engine: pattern detection runs incrementally on new output (O(new rows), not O(total)), so thousands of live links cost ~nothing as the stream grows.
  • Open IDE protocol: navigation is newline-delimited JSON over a local TCP socket (a backend plugin resolves files/symbols + moves the caret on 8765; a frontend plugin scrolls the viewport + reports the caret on 8766). Any editor can implement it; see the API spec. JetBrains today; VS Code / Neovim / Emacs welcome.
  • Cross-platform shell: WSL on Windows, native PTY on macOS.

Open protocols

Each capability is a small, documented protocol, not a feature sealed in the app.

  • IDE navigation: the local-socket protocol above; any editor can implement it.
  • Review: the agent writes a markdown review that organizes and explains the diff, per the open agent-threads spec; agent-term renders it and carries your inline comments back to the agent. Other hosts welcome.
  • Viewers by URL: one convention routes whatever the agent prints. A review:// link auto-opens the rendered review, http(s) opens the embedded web viewer, and a markdown file renders with the same inline commenting. The URL is the whole API: an agent needs no SDK to drive the host; it prints a line of text.
  • Fleet coordination: a lock / ownership / HEAD-guard convention so many agents can share one checkout without clobbering each other (agent-lock).
  • Conventions by filename: agents bind to docs by name, resolving to the nearest such file up the directory tree (commit-message.md, the kits' config; agent-cicd's CONFIG shows the rule). No central config. agent-term itself just listens for the references: a proceed-by-branching.md going by is its cue to start watching the work branch and lock.
  • Voice input: a source injects a raw speech-to-text transcript prefixed with a pointer to a vendored guide (voice-to-agent); the agent, holding the whole session, reconstructs the dictation against context and acts, so no hub-side model has to.

Install

  • Windows: download the installer (AgentTerm-x.x.x-setup.exe) from the Releases page. Requires WSL; your agents run in it.
  • macOS (from source): git clone https://github.com/albertwujj/agent-term && cd agent-term && npm install && npm run start. That first npm run start is the only one: from then on Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+N opens the next window, and closing the last window respawns a fresh one, so AgentTerm keeps itself running. To close it for good, type exit.

These are the paths we run daily and verify with each release. If setup snags anywhere, ask your agent to fix it.

  • IDE plugins (for click-to-IDE): the two intellij-navigator zips are on the same Releases page, with step-by-step install in the release notes.
  • Phone/web viewer: self-host agent-stream-hub and add it to your home screen.

Shortcuts

The few worth learning (Ctrl on Windows, Cmd on Mac):

  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+N: a new AgentTerm window, opening on the session picker. This is the only kind of new: every session is a whole OS window, and there are no tabs.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+U: everything the session can open in a viewer (docs, images, URLs), as a filterable list.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O / +I: grow / shrink the open viewer.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+F: fuzzy-search the whole scrollback.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+K: insert your IDE's current location into the prompt.

Related repos

  • agent-term (this repo): the host that extends the terminal.
  • agent-stream-hub: the phone/web viewer + relay.
  • intellij-navigator: JetBrains plugins (file/symbol nav + the read-only guard).

Plus the open specs (bring your own host/agent):

  • agent-threads: the review-thread spec the review loop (and live-markdown commenting) runs on.
  • agent-lock: a lock so several agents share one git checkout without clobbering each other (the working tree, branches, and the host-global ports their tests grab).
  • agent-cicd: scripts that watch a Gerrit change's Jenkins build to a verdict and auto-retry infra flakes, pushes serialized through agent-lock; the kits composing in practice.
  • voice-to-agent: the vendored guide that tells an agent to reconstruct and act on a raw speech-to-text transcript (what the phone's voice input runs on).

Built with Electron · xterm.js (WebGL) · node-pty · esbuild. MIT licensed. A ⭐ helps others find it.

blocks.html_en: How it works (for the curious)

sentences.en: How it works (for the curious)
sentences.zh: 它是如何工作的（对于好奇的人来说）

blocks.html_en: • One click rule: a plain click opens what renders in-app (markdown, reviews, web pages, images); anything that hands you to another application (OS apps, your IDE) waits for Ctrl/Cmd; commenting always goes through a selection.

sentences.en: One click rule: a plain click opens what renders in-app (markdown, reviews, web pages, images); anything that hands you to another application (OS apps, your IDE) waits for Ctrl/Cmd; commenting always goes through a selection.
sentences.zh: 一键规则：只需单击即可打开应用内呈现的内容（Markdown、评论、网页、图像）；任何将你转到另一个应用程序（操作系统应用程序、IDE）的东西都等待 Ctrl/Cmd；评论总是要经过选择的。

blocks.html_en: • Append-only, single-pass decoration engine: pattern detection runs incrementally on new output (O(new rows), not O(total)), so thousands of live links cost ~nothing as the stream grows.

sentences.en: Append-only, single-pass decoration engine: pattern detection runs incrementally on new output (O(new rows), not O(total)), so thousands of live links cost ~nothing as the stream grows.
sentences.zh: 仅附加、单通道装饰引擎：模式检测在新输出上增量运行（O（新行），而不是 O（总计）），因此随着流的增长，数千个实时链接几乎不需要任何成本。

blocks.html_en: • Open IDE protocol: navigation is newline-delimited JSON over a local TCP socket (a backend plugin resolves files/symbols + moves the caret on 8765; a frontend plugin scrolls the viewport + reports the caret on 8766). Any editor can implement it; see the API spec. JetBrains today; VS Code / Neovim / Emacs welcome.

sentences.en: Open IDE protocol: navigation is newline-delimited JSON over a local TCP socket (a backend plugin resolves files/symbols + moves the caret on 8765; a frontend plugin scrolls the viewport + reports the caret on 8766).
sentences.zh: 开放 IDE 协议：导航是本地 TCP 套接字上的换行符分隔的 JSON（后端插件解析文件/符号 + 在 8765 上移动插入符号；前端插件滚动视口 + 报告 8766 上的插入符号）。

sentences.en: Any editor can implement it; see the API spec.
sentences.zh: 任何编辑器都可以实现；请参阅 API 规范。

sentences.en: JetBrains today; VS Code / Neovim / Emacs welcome.

content_html_zh:
代理期限

驾驶您已经运行的一组编码代理：在终端之外，在您已经熟悉的表面上。

与任何 CLI 编码代理（Claude Code、Codex 等）一起使用。

编码代理选择终端的原因是：没有什么比它更灵活了，一切都可以用它来组合。 但终端从未赶上代理的发展。 代理打印的所有内容（差异、计划、声明、链接）都是死文本，您可以阅读但无法执行操作。 一旦你运行了几个，每个外面都是一个相同的选项卡，里面都是一堵文本墙，不知道你想返回哪个。 AgentTerm 保持基础并突破天花板：根据代理打印的内容采取行动，审查其构建的内容直至正确，找到正确的会话，在运行中进行引导。 当采用尚不存在的约定时，它将它们定义为开放协议：代理打印一个 review:// 链接，并且评论将在终端中打开。

指向代理向您显示的任何内容（一行终端输出或差异）并说出您想要的内容；代理人进行更改。

找到合适的会议

运行多个代理，AgentTerm 在两个级别上跟踪它们。 您正在积极操作的按钮变成了 Windows 任务栏按钮，每个按钮都有一个工作指示器和两个级别的实时预览，显示会话的用途和正在执行的操作。 （在 Mac 上，全屏运行每个会话：每个窗口将其初始提示固定在顶部，可通过任务控制滑动读取。） 您预留的内容只需按一下按键即可：打开选择器并根据您询问的内容或代理所称的工作来过滤您过去的会话，而更深层次的搜索则会搜索您输入的每个提示；恢复其中任何一个（上面的英雄）。 无需通过相似的终端进行搜索，也无需与代理来回寻找。

通过手机观看和驾驶

将配套查看器 (agent-stream-hub) 作为 Web 应用程序添加到手机的主屏幕。 它显示哪些代理需要您在所有机器上（“轮到您”），并像终端本身一样深入到任何实时会话：与您留在办公桌上的屏幕相同，一目了然，甚至其菜单也可按键驱动。 通过语音引导：说话，您的话语会以文本形式到达代理，它知道来自语音，因此它会在行动之前修复会话中的听错和错误开始。 这是电话听写无法做到的部分：在看不到代码的情况下，它会听到“馅饼测试”并将其留在那里；代理将其转换为 pytest。 即使是从仅允许出站 HTTPS 的网络，也应改为键入。

   

再加上生活质量的东西

将图像和拖放文件直接粘贴到提示中 · 模糊搜索整个回滚 · 单击代理打印的图像路径并在应用程序中直接呈现（按住 Ctrl/Cmd 并单击将 .pdf、.csv、文件夹和其余内容发送到其操作系统应用程序） · 右键单击​​将选择引用到提示中。 Ctrl+K / Cmd+K 将 IDE 的当前位置插入提示符中。

评论其输出

代理告诉您的大部分内容都会在终端中滚动过去。 选择其中任何一个（一行、一个声明、一个即将运行的命令）并发表评论；您的便条将返回给代理，并附有引用的确切文本，因此几句话就足够了。 （也适用于渲染的 Markdown 查看器。）

如果您的 CLI 捕获了鼠标（Claude Code 的全屏渲染捕获了鼠标），请在选择时按住 Shift；评论的作用是一样的。 要保持普通拖动选择，请使用 CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 启动 Claude Code，或使用 CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS=1 来保持滚轮滚动。

......以及代理收到的内容：您的话，并引用确切的上下文：

审查，而不是差异之墙

当代理完成后，它会准备您的审查：它会向您提供需要您判断的部分，并进行排序和解释，并标记权衡，并忽略不需要的部分：机械噪音（重命名、导入、样板文件）以及您在会话期间已经解决的问题。 对代码及其推理进行内嵌评论；它会在线程中编辑、回复，然后评论会重新呈现。

与它一起计划

观看者将 Markdown 变成了你实时写英语的地方。 文档会在代理工作时打开并呈现并更新。 对任何段落进行评论，或直接编辑渲染的文本，在任何地方开始新行；编辑作为建议到达代理，它决定源中每个新行的内容（标题、列表项、段落）。 您在预览中编写，从不接触原始降价或切换编辑/预览模式，并且代理维护源。

英语才是真正计划发生的地方。 设计的很大一部分是在任何代码之前用文字解决的：计划、设计文档、结果。 这些文档是您如何与代理合作以及如何与其他人合作的方式。 他们以这种方式制作的速度如此之快，以至于一个项目可以为每个受众提供一份有针对性的文档：针对代理商、针对开发人员、针对项目经理等等。 该计划以代码的方式进行聚合：评论、就地修改、在构建任何内容之前解决。 同样的循环涵盖任何写作项目（论文、笔记、研究、文档）：您的材料被组织为存储库，代理根据需要使用并为您编辑。

确认代理告诉您的内容

代理通过引用 file:line 和符号来解释自己。 按住 Ctrl 键并单击代理提到的任何引用（在 Mac 上为 Cmd；不仅仅是它编辑的文件），您的 IDE 会跳转到该行，以便您可以验证声明。 它引用的 URL 也可以在终端的嵌入式 Web 视图中打开。

看看不破坏它

默认情况下，您的 IDE 编辑器保持只读状态，因此您不必担心误击按键。 （在极少数情况下您想直接编辑，请翻转设置。）

让它成为你的

这里的一切都是模块化的和代理大小的：终端是 18k 行纯 JS (MIT)，IDE 插件、手机查看器和审查规范都是它们自己的小存储库。 拿起你想要的那件，把它变成你自己的。 分享您构建的内容，并借鉴其他人所做的内容。

平台

在 macOS 和 Windows 上运行。 AgentTerm 是使用 AgentTerm 本身在 Mac 上构建的，并且大量用于 Windows 上的工作，因此两者都是一流的。 实时会话切换与 Windows 任务栏集成。 在 Mac 上，为每个会话提供自己的全屏或桌面：初始提示固定在窗口顶部，因此任务控制滑动会显示每个会话，可读（欢迎更针对 Mac 优化的 UX）。 目前 IDE 导航的目标是 JetBrains，但该协议是开放的，因此可以轻松添加其他编辑器和代码查看器。 公关在这两个方面都受到欢迎。 全部 MIT，全部免费：没有遥测，没有追加销售。

它是如何工作的（对于好奇的人来说）

  • 一键规则：只需单击即可打开应用内呈现的内容（Markdown、评论、网页、图像）；任何将你转到另一个应用程序（操作系统应用程序、IDE）的东西都等待 Ctrl/Cmd；评论总是要经过选择的。
  • 仅附加、单通道装饰引擎：模式检测在新输出上增量运行（O（新行），而不是 O（总计）），因此随着流的增长，数千个实时链接几乎不需要任何成本。
  • 开放 IDE 协议：导航是本地 TCP 套接字上的换行符分隔的 JSON（后端插件解析文件/符号 + 在 8765 上移动插入符号；前端插件滚动视口 + 报告 8766 上的插入符号）。 任何编辑器都可以实现；请参阅 API 规范。 今天的 JetBrains；欢迎使用 VS Code / Neovim / Emacs。
  • 跨平台 shell：Windows 上的 WSL，macOS 上的本机 PTY。

开放协议

每个功能都是一个小型的、记录在案的协议，而不是应用程序中密封的功能。

  • IDE导航：上面的本地套接字协议；任何编辑器都可以实现它。
  • 审查：代理根据开放代理线程规范编写一个 Markdown 审查来组织和解释差异； agent-term 呈现它并将您的内联评论返回给代理。 欢迎其他主持人。
  • 通过 URL 查看者：一种约定会路由代理打印的任何内容。 review:// 链接自动打开呈现的评论，http(s) 打开嵌入式 Web 查看器，并且使用相同的内联注释呈现 Markdown 文件。 URL是整个API：代理不需要SDK来驱动主机；它打印一行文本。
  • 车队协调：一种锁/所有权/HEAD-guard 约定，因此许多代理可以共享一个结账而不会互相破坏（代理锁）。
  • 按文件名约定：代理按名称绑定到文档，解析到目录树中最近的此类文件（commit-message.md，套件的配置；agent-cicd 的 CONFIG 显示规则）。 没有中央配置。 agent-term 本身只是监听引用：一个proceed-by-branching.md 的经过是它开始监视工作分支和锁定的提示。
  • 语音输入：源注入原始语音到文本的转录本，前缀为指向供应商指南（语音到代理）的指针；代理负责整个会话，根据上下文和行为重建听写，因此中心端模型不必这样做。

安装

  • Windows：从发布页面下载安装程序 (AgentTerm-x.x.x-setup.exe)。 需要 WSL；你的代理人在其中运行。
  • macOS（来自源代码）： git clone https://github.com/albertwujj/agent-term && cd agent-term && npm install && npm run start。 第一个 npm run start 是唯一的一个：从那时起 Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+N 打开下一个窗口，关闭最后一个窗口会重新生成一个新窗口，因此 AgentTerm 保持自身运行。 要永久关闭它，请输入 exit。

这些是我们每天运行并在每个版本中验证的路径。 如果设置在任何地方出现问题，请要求您的代理进行修复。

  • IDE 插件（用于点击 IDE）：两个 intellij-navigator zip 位于同一版本页面上，并在发行说明中逐步安装。
  • 电话/网络查看器：自行托管 agent-stream-hub 并将其添加到您的主屏幕。

快捷方式

几个值得学习的（Windows 上的 Ctrl，Mac 上的 Cmd）：

  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+N：一个新的 AgentTerm 窗口，在会话选择器上打开。 这是唯一的新功能：每个会话都是一个完整的操作系统窗口，并且没有选项卡。
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+U：会话可以在查看器中打开的所有内容（文档、图像、URL），作为可过滤列表。
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O / +I：放大/缩小打开的查看器。
  • Ctrl/Cmd+F：模糊搜索整个回滚。
  • Ctrl/Cmd+K：将 IDE 的当前位置插入提示符中。

相关仓库

  • agent-term（本存储库）：扩展终端的主机。
  • agent-stream-hub：电话/网络查看器 + 中继。
  • intellij-navigator：JetBrains 插件（文件/符号导航 + 只读防护）。

加上开放规格（带上您自己的主机/代理）：

  • 代理线程：审阅循环（和实时 Markdown 评论）运行的审阅线程规范。
  • agent-lock：一种锁，因此多个代理共享一个 git checkout 而不会互相破坏（工作树、分支以及它们的测试抓取的主机全局端口）。
